2.  26-53994  Recommendation to approve the Scoring and Ranking Policies for the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care Portfolio.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Department of Health staff Joseph Botelho provided updates to the revisions
  on the Scoring and Ranking Policies, staff identified areas within the policies
  that required updates. On the Score and Methodology section, there was
  clarification on the reporting periods and exemptions, narrative was aligned
  to ensure clarity of calculations and policy application. Misaligned metric
  cutoffs and calculations were corrected along with project type totals.
  • The board was provided copy of the changes made along with the final
  version of the updates policies.
  • Members of the board and staff engage in discussion regarding the updates
  discussed.

3.  26-53995  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on updates for the FY 2025
  Continuum of Care (CoC) Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).

  A motion was made by Member Rockenbach, seconded by Member
  McFadzen, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None

  Page 2 of 7
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 13, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

  Absent:  3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Department of Health staff Joseph Botelho provided updates on the FY 2025
  CoC Program NOFO. Jospeh discussed the competition timeline, HUD
  released the FY 2025 CoC NOFO on November 13, 2025, on December 8,
  2025 HUD withdrew the NOFO to make revisions and issue a modified
  version, on January 9, 2026 HUD reopened the FY 24-25 NOFO with
  guidance to process renewals. There is approximately $3.524 billion in
  funding available.
  • Staff move to discuss the two pathways for renewal under the FY 24-25
  NOFO. Pathway 1: Projects funded in FY 2024 that are not reallocated or
  replaced may be eligible for FY 2025 selection using the FY 2024
  submission with written confirmation from Collaborative Applicant, Pathway
  2: If submitting renewals not funded in FY 2024 and/or new projects created
  through reallocation, the CoC must complete project applications in e-snaps
  and submit a FY 2025 Priority Listing.
  • Staff will develop and begin implementing a timeline for all key NOFO
  activities, and monitor HUD updates and related litigation/court orders.
  • Staff and Board Members are in agreement that path 1 is the best option.
  • A member of the public comments regarding the current NOFO application
  and process.

4.  26-53996  Recommendation to discuss the scope of and establish the Continuum of Care
  Governance Ad Hoc Workgroup, and if appropriate, appoint members.

  A motion was made by Co-Chair Diles III, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided a brief overview
  of the requirements of the Brown Act and Robert’s Rules of Order. In light of
  recent reviews of the Governance Charter, staff recommended the formation
  of an Ad Hoc committee work group consisting of members Diles, Amick,
  and McFadzen.
  • The work group would meet up to three times during the year, with meetings
  held virtually, to review and finalize the Governance Charter.
  • A member of the public asked how the public would be notified of the Ad Hoc

5.  26-53997  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion regarding the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care (CoC) new Board member solicitation.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Health Department Staff Joseph Botelho provided updates regarding the two
  open seats on the board. Staff are recommending that applications reopen
  beginning January 14, 2026- February 11,2026 due to limited submissions.
  • Requirements to fill these seats have been posted online and sent via email.

6.  26-54008  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation from the Domestic Violence
  Homeless Services Coalition (DVHSC) and the Homeless Equity for Left Behind
  Populations (HELP) Act from Downtown Women's Center and Rainbow Services.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Jetzel Chavez, DV Regional Coordinator at Rainbow Services and Cristina
  Cortes, Sr. Manager DVHSC, Downtown Women’s center provided a
  presentation on the intersection of gender-based violence and
  homelessness.
  • DVHSC Core team partners is the body that dictates what they are doing in
  the near future, and includes partners like LAHSA, Rainbow Services and
  Downtown Women’s Center to name a few.

  Page 4 of 7
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 13, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

  • Most data is domestic violence focused, as there is a lack of data on sexual
  assault and human trafficking.
  • 12% of people are experiencing homelessness have experienced domestic
  violence, 65% are unhoused and 10.5% of people experiencing
  homelessness due to abuse.
  • Members of the Board raised questions regarding how data is collected,
  specifically whether and how it is linked to funding.
  • HELP Act aims to reduce homelessness among domestic violence survivors,
  their children, and unaccompanied women. In 2024, more than 74,000
  domestic violence survivors, 24,000 children survivors, and 98,000
  unaccompanied women accessed homelessness services in California.
  • There are less than 1,000 interim housing beds or survivors, in 2025 the PIT
  reported 3,546 unsheltered adults in need of DV specific bed.
  • There are 3 PSH sites. SB 194 mandates to ensure inclusion of women and
  survivors in all state-funded homelessness plans.
  • DVHSC will be connecting with local cities in the coming months to
  understand how survivors’ needs are being incorporated, in accordance with
  the HELP ACT.
  • Member Martins expressed interest in connecting with Jetzel to explore
  potential support through the VA. Member Hawk commented on the
  importance of ensuring that services are inclusive and extended to
  individuals who identify as non-binary.

7.  26-53999  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion regarding the Homeless Services
  Bureau funding landscape.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member McFadzen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Health Department Staff Jeffrey Proctor provided funding updates and a
  clear view on risks, impacts, and planning considerations.
  Funding and Policy Environment Updates
  • Federal: Uncertainty related to HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) funding,
  potential shifts in Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) policies, delays in
  the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO), ongoing litigation, and risks
  associated with Tier 1 and Tier 2 reallocation.State: Upcoming expiration of

  Page 5 of 7
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 13, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

  HHAP, ERF, and Homekey programs.
  • County: Potential Measure A CoC funding reductions under consideration,
  as well as the expiration and closeout of Measure H.
  • Philanthropy: Limited funding scale and decreasing flexibility.
  Risk Scenarios
  • A overview of County Measure A CoC and HUD CoC were discussed.
  • Core system functions impacted would include Shelter and interim housing
  capacity and Rapid Rehousing and prevention slots.
  • Measure A CoC funds offset volatility from other sources and maintain
  continuity during delays and transitions.
  • If reductions occur the main focus include prioritizing life-safety and housing
  stability, protect compliance and system performance, minimize service
  disruptions, and center equity and high-risk populations.
  • In the next coming weeks staff are looking for CoC Board and General
  Membership alignment during a special meeting.

8.  26-54010  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff and
  Operations Update presentation from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Amick, seconded by Member McFadzen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Scott, Lowery-Luyties, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided bureau staff updates including the
  Project Homekey at 5950 Long Beach Blvd. that began operations in early
  December. 20 beds have been set aside as part of the initial effort on the
  Encampment Resoultion Fund (ERF).
  • Staff are working with the Los Angeles County Affordable Housing Solutions
  Agency (LACAHSA) around new homeless prevention programming
  requirements and setups.
  • Staff and the Office of Homeless Strategy and Partnership are working on a
  new strategic plan focused on youth.
  • The Point In Time count is set to take place January 22, 2026, at 4:30 a.m.,
  teams will be mobilizing from The Grand Long Beach.

  TUESDAY, JANUARY 13, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 3:00 PM

9.  26-54019  Recommendation to recieve and file the Homeless Services Advisory Committee
  representative updates.

  A motion was made by Member Shuford, seconded by Member McFadzen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  12 Lowery-Luyties, Scott, Wee, Shuford, Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Diles III, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff

  • Member Pat Scott provided updates on the shower truck recently purchased
  by the city. Logistics and scheduling for the mobile showers are still being
  finalized, and the committee is continuing to gather additional information
  regarding their use.
  • The committee is also working on a pilot program for trash cleanup services
  and exploring ways to assist in providing additional safe locations to meet
  the basic needs of unhoused individuals.
  • Members of the baord provided feedback regarding this discussion.
  • A member of the public suggested that the committee explore providing
  lockers for the unhoused.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • A member of the public raised a comment regarding lockers.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • No announcements.
